To clarify: 

33 Thomas St is not owned by the NSA but has obviously been associated with 3-letter agency intel collection activities. Nearly all of your tech providers provide services for intel agencies. As for its off-putting look, it's built for functionality. Windows are liabilities for sig leakage, blast resistance, EMP, etc. Fewer entries simply increase physical security. It's not a building that was built to be inhabited by a bunch of workers but it has to be able to support and protect sensitive tech and personnel in any scenario.

NSA doesn't 'tap' telecom, Google, etc, they work with them willingly and you'd be silly believe otherwise or think it's unnecessary. TITANPOINTE alleged NSA presence inside such ATT facilities, which includes 33 Thomas St but that doesn't suggest the NSA owns or controls it. Any intel presence in there would be compartmented or leased and obviously not overt. Reporting has exaggerated all these theories. It is not a gov datacenter but it is a telecom switching and routing hub which does have intelligence value when you're talking access to in-transit data.

Also keep in mind, Snowden's access and leaks were just as exaggerated. Take it with a grain of salt. He had consequential access and his leaks were on real, unknown NSA + partner programs but he did not have access to, or context for, everything so much of the use case for such programs is speculative. He was a contracted sysadmin and did not own any particular program.. broad visibility sure, but shallow access. Someone in his position would have access to some architectures and docs, maybe some repos, and could see how things worked but they sure as shit do not see everything being collected.

The public image of the NSA being god-like is silly. They're very capable, sure, but NSA isn't casually spying on John and Jane Smith. So no, this is not a super villain lair. It's surely a menacing building if you only ingest the conspiracy hype.
